finding.claim: Unvalidated SSRF in /fetch: the target query parameter is passed directly to http.Get and the full response body is returned to the caller.

trace.note: http.ListenAndServe(":8080", nil) exposes the server on all interfaces
/fetch is registered to the fetch handler
target is read from the query string with no processing
http.Get issues the request with no checks
io.Copy returns the full response body to the attacker, so this is a full-read SSRF

finding.guards_checked: None. No scheme, host, IP/private-range, port, or redirect restrictions, and no authentication on the endpoint.

verdict.reason: main.go:15-16 passes the unauthenticated query parameter target directly to http.Get and main.go:22 returns the full body; the allowlist at main.go:9-12 is only enforced in safeFetch (main.go:27), which is routed at /safe (main.go:42), not /fetch (main.go:41).

finding.claim: Allowlist bypass via redirect in /safe: the hostname allowlist is checked only on the initial URL, and the default http.Get client follows up to 10 redirects, so an allowed host can redirect to an internal or metadata address. Conditional on an allowed host returning such a redirect.

trace.note: /safe is registered to the safeFetch handler
allowed[u.Hostname()] is checked against images.example.org and docs.example.org
http.Get uses the default client, which follows redirects with no CheckRedirect; the allowlist is not re-checked on redirect targets
the final response body is copied back to the caller

finding.guards_checked: url.Parse error handling at main.go:27 is correct. u.Hostname() strips userinfo and port, so userinfo tricks are blocked. Scheme is not checked, but http.Get only performs http/https. No CheckRedirect on the client. Hostnames are not resolved and checked against private/link-local IPs, so DNS names pointing internally would pass. Exploitability depends on whether the allowed hosts have open redirects, which cannot be confirmed from this repo.

verdict.guard_found: Exact hostname membership on the parsed hostname at main.go:27 (`allowed[u.Hostname()]`), applied only to the initial URL. No CheckRedirect on the default client, and no re-check of redirect targets before or after the http.Get at main.go:31.
verdict.reason: Every trace line checks out: /safe is registered at main.go:42, target is parsed at main.go:26, the exact-hostname allowlist is at main.go:27, http.Get at main.go:31 follows redirects by default, and the body is copied back at main.go:37. The source is attacker-controlled (main.go:26), but the bypass only works if images.example.org or docs.example.org returns a redirect to an internal or metadata address, and that behavior is external to this repo, so the claim cannot be confirmed or refuted from the code.
